title: Minimum Operations to Convert Number
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums containing distinct numbers, an integer start, and an integer goal, determine the minimum number of operations needed to convert start to goal.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums containing distinct numbers, an integer start, and an integer goal, determine the minimum number of operations needed to convert start to goal. You can perform operations on a number x (initially set to start) by adding, subtracting, or performing a bitwise XOR with any element in nums. Each element in nums can be used any number of times in any order. If the result of an operation is outside the range 0 to 1000, the operation is still valid, but no more operations can be performed afterward. If it is not possible to convert start to goal, return -1.
constraints: nums contains distinct integers; start is within 0..1000 and goal may be outside.
From x, one step may produce x+v, x-v, or x xor v for any v in nums.
An out-of-range result may equal goal but cannot be expanded; return minimum steps or -1.
hints: The bounded expandable values form an unweighted graph, with the possibly out-of-range goal checked as a terminal neighbor.
BFS from start; generate plus, minus, and xor results, return immediately on goal, and enqueue unseen in-range results.
Queue (value,steps); test candidate==goal before the 0..1000 expansion guard.
BFS explores operation counts in increasing order, and the guard matches the rule that outside results are terminal.
editorial: BFS explores operation counts in increasing order, and the guard matches the rule that outside results are terminal.

tests.explanation: A shortest sequence reaches twelve in two operations.
Subtracting values can reach the outside-range goal in two operations.
